extracted.intended_audience: approved Flipboard curators, creators, publishers, and brands
extracted.subtask_description: Platform-specific best practices for creating finite, theme-based Storyboards on Flipboard that inform, inspire, and entertain — aimed at approved curators seeking discoverability, traffic, and editorial features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and nature of Storyboards (finite, definitive collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Storyboards are an exciting way for approved curators to package together content that informs, inspires and entertains audiences. Unlike Magazines, which are designed for ongoing curation, Storyboards are designed to be finite and definitive collections that can be shared on and off Flipboard to reach new audiences, drive traffic and gain new followers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Storyboards as a bounded, shareable package with a clear beginning and end (not an ongoing magazine). The editorial team looks for Storyboards to feature in Today’s Picks, Explore, email campaigns, and other programming; design Storyboards with discoverability and shareability in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curate the highest quality journalism across news and lifestyle
rubrics_metrics.description: Curate the highest quality journalism across news and lifestyle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer well-written pieces with a strong and compelling narrative; select in-depth pieces that provide a unique angle; include important coverage around a current event or issue. Aim for journalism that informs, inspires, or entertains and that fits the Storyboard’s theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help readers go deeper — thematic coherence and minimum items
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a minimum of five items in a Storyboard that connect around a theme; helping the reader go deep on a topic, learn more about an event or get the full story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Storyboard should have at least five items that collectively allow readers to explore the topic in depth. Items should share a clear thematic connection and together offer new insights or perspectives and enrich a reader’s understanding of the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sections to organize content (section size limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sections to further organize your content and make it easier to browse (note: each section can hold up to 10 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break the Storyboard into coherent sections to improve scannability and navigation. Keep each section to at most 10 items to avoid overwhelming readers and to maintain clear structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a main image that is related to the overall theme, not just a single article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a cover/main image that represents the Storyboard’s theme as a whole (avoid picking an image that only reflects one item). The image should support the narrative and entice clicks/shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select relevant topic tags (use up to five)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider selecting all five topic tags (max) recommended by Flipboard to increase relevancy and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply up to five topic tags to maximize relevance and distribution across Flipboard. Choose tags that accurately reflect the Storyboard’s subject matter to improve discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use language to set the right expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the title and description to tell the reader what is in the collection, setting their expectations and enticing them to read more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft title and description that clearly explain what the Storyboard contains and what the reader will get. Ensure each item in the Storyboard supports the narrative framed in the title and description so users aren’t confused or disappointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an original and engaging title and description (accurate numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be descriptive and capture your brand voice. Title should be article-like and any numbers in the title should reflect the number of stories in the Storyboard (note: using the headline of a single listicle in the collection confuses the user about what’s in the Storyboard. If the Storyboard is titled “53 Weeknight Meals” users expect 53 items in the collection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write an original, article-style title that matches the collection (avoid reusing a single listicle headline unless the count/contents match). Include relevant keywords in the description to increase discoverability and convey brand voice.
